Description: A torus built from nothing but two exact circles in NURBS form: a rational quadratic circle of radius 8 as the profile and a second one of radius 30 as the sweep path. Both are given by control points, knot vector and weights - the classical nine pole representation of four 90 degree arcs with the corner weights sqrt(2)/2 - so they are circles in the exact sense and not approximations of one. Nothing in the case is a primitive: there is no Ellipse, no ToroidalSurface and no solid.torus anywhere in it, and that is the point. It is the smallest input that forces solid.sweep into the general case - a path that is neither a straight line nor a circular arc object - while still having a result whose volume can be written down by hand.
Expected:
One closed solid, the torus with R = 30 and r = 8. Volume 2*pi^2*R*r^2 = 2*pi^2*30*64 = 37899.2809, area 4*pi^2*R*r = 4*pi^2*240 = 9474.8202, extent -38, -38, -8 .. 38, 38, 8. Both numbers are calculated, not measured. The volume must come out positive: a swept solid with a reversed shell is a defect that has been seen before in this corpus (HelicalExtrudeOrientationUnstable), and the sign is the cheapest test for it. The band in the assertion of call 9 is deliberately wider below the exact value than above it, because a triangulated volume underestimates a curved body and never exceeds it. The topology is NOT pinned by this prose: how many faces the sweep produces, and whether the swept surface ends up as a NurbsSurface, a SweptCircle or a recognized ToroidalSurface, is the implementation's choice - the recorded fingerprint will say which, once there is one.
MEASURED 2026-09-16: volume 37899.2808124 and area 9474.82020311, both matching the calculated values above; extent exact. The topology turned out to be four SweptCurveSurface faces with no caps - the path closes, so there is no start or end face - and the surface is NOT recognized as a torus, which was left open above as the implementation's choice.
Status:
Green since 2026-09-16. Both blockers are gone, and a third one that only showed up on the way.
(1) sketch.add_nurbs ignored control points. NurbsFromControlPoints in ShapeIt/MCPServer.cs now builds the curve from poles, the flat knot vector and the weights, compressing [0,0,0,1,1,2,2,3,3,4,4,4] into knots [0,1,2,3,4] with multiplicities [3,2,2,2,3] for BSpline2D. Both circles are exact - sampled at 201 parameters the radius holds to 7e-15.
(2) solid.sweep could not sweep along anything but a line or a circular arc. Make3D.ExtrudeCurveToFace now builds a CADability.GeoObject.SweptCurveSurface where it used to return null - the class that replaced GeneralSweptCurve, which could not even be constructed on an ordinary curve. The face is the whole unit square of that surface, its outline counterclockwise so that the normal comes out as the direction of the profile crossed with the direction of the spine, which is the orientation the other branches produce and the one SewFaces needs.
(3) MakePipe took the path apart with along.Curves and swept each part as it came. A closed CURVE among them cannot work: the face swept from it meets itself at v = 0 = 1, and its boundary comes out as one closed edge - the thing SplitSingleOutlines exists to prevent for the profile. Such a part is now split at 0.5, the same way a single closed profile curve already was. The test is geometric and NOT ICurve.IsClosed: for a BSpline that property returns the 'periodic' flag, and this case's clamped nine pole circle answers false to it. Getting that wrong the first time is what produced a two face torus with two closed edges and consistent = false.
A fourth defect was mine and is worth recording because it is a trap for any surface whose curves point back at it: SweptCurveSurface.FixedU used to hand out curves that read the surface they came from. ISurfaceImpl lets a surface be changed in place, and Shell does call ReverseOrientation on faces while sewing - which then displaced edges that had already been built, by the extent of the profile, leaving edges that no longer met their own vertices. FixedU now builds on a copy of the surface.
THE RECORDED NUMBERS ARE EXACT, which is the point of a case built from nothing but exact circles: volume 37899.2808124 against the calculated 2*pi^2*30*64 = 37899.2809, a relative 2e-9, and area 9474.82020311 against 4*pi^2*240 = 9474.8202. The extent is exact, the shell is consistent and closed, and V - E + F = 4 - 8 + 4 = 0 is the Euler characteristic of a torus. There are no start and end faces because the path closes and comes back with the same direction, so MakePipe leaves them out.
The one line that is NOT exact is edgeLength, 467.975 against 477.522: the eight edges are four halves of the profile circle plus the two boundary circles at r = 38 and r = 22, and ICurve.Length of a rational spline is the chord polygon through its spans rather than the arc length. Same defect the companion case RuledSolidsFromNurbsCircles documents. When it is fixed, this line moves up and the case goes red - which is then the fix showing itself, not a regression.
Note:
A NURBS curve IS usable as a sweep path - the toolset does not have to grow a new parameter for it. solid.sweep takes 'path' as a NameRef and resolves it through GetSketchCurves, which reads the sketch from the curve's UserData[MCPServer.Sketch] and maps the 2d curve to 3d with curve2D.MakeGeoObject(sketch.Plane). Any named sketch curve therefore serves as the path, in any sketch, and the profile does not have to live in the same sketch as the path - here it deliberately does not. What the description of solid.sweep calls 'a 3D curve or polycurve' is exactly this: sketch curves are the only source of 3d curves the toolset has.
The profile sketch is placed so that its plane contains the path's start point (30, 0, 0) and is perpendicular to the path's tangent there (the tangent is +y, the plane spans +x and +z). MakePipe does reposition a single planar profile face onto the path start, but only along the path - it does not reorient a profile that starts out skew, so a case that wants an exact torus has to place the profile correctly itself.

params.message: the sweep of an exact circle r = 8 along an exact circle R = 30 is a torus with V = 2*pi^2*R*r^2 = 37899.2809; a triangulated volume stays slightly below that, a negative or wildly different value means the shell is reversed or the sweep is wrong
